findings.title: Legacy pre-120 `sq_run` entries without a run id can crash the resident process on the Runner's first tick
findings.description:
`_in_flight_run_ids` reads `entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID]` with `[]`. Pre-slice-120 entries carry no `run_id` parameter (that is why `SquadronRunObserver` routes them to the legacy matcher, `src/amoeba/process/observers/sq_run_id.py`). If recovery's legacy matcher leaves such an entry `InFlight` (unresolved, which is what "left in flight for its issuer" means), the sequence on the next tick is:

1. `ProjectTick._run_entries` filters only on `kind is CommandKind.SQ_RUN` — the legacy entry qualifies.
2. `RunObserver._observe_one` (src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:110-113) raises `ValueError` because `run_id` is not a string.
3. `RunnerTenant._tick_project`'s broad catch logs and calls `escalate(store, project_id, context, ...)` with the entry's node in context.
4. `escalate` calls `_in_flight_run_ids(store, project_id, node.id)`, which finds the same legacy entry and does `entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID]` → `KeyError`.

That `KeyError` is raised *inside* the `except Exception` handler, so it propagates out of `RunnerTenant.tick` entirely — it is neither in `STORE_FAILURES` nor `UpstreamShapeError` — and kills the resident process with an unhandled traceback, on every restart, since recovery will keep leaving the entry in flight. Either `_in_flight_run_ids` should use `.get(PARAM_RUN_ID)` and skip non-string values (as `_observe_one` itself models), or `_run_entries` should exclude entries without a usable run id so they never reach the observer.

findings.title: `_link` test helper is imported across test modules as a private name
findings.description: `from runner.test_probes import _link  # pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]` reaches into another test module's private helper. `_link` creates a CF link submission against a store and belongs in a shared support module (`tests/runner/` already has `observe_support.py` / `tick_support.py` for exactly this) so the `pyright: ignore` isn't needed and the dependency between test files is explicit rather than suppressed.

findings.title: `build_argv` is executed twice per launch
findings.description: `ProjectTick._launch` calls `build_argv(...)` purely to raise `ValueError` before journaling, then `launch()` rebuilds the identical argv from the journaled entry. The duplication is deliberate (validate-before-write is the right order) and the second build is what actually runs, so the two can never disagree for a *committed* entry — but a comment in `_launch` saying the pre-call is validation-only, mirroring the one already in `launch`, would make the intent unmistakable.

findings.title: Budget, fault and escalation discipline is mechanically enforced
findings.description: The load-bearing invariants all have dedicated tests: `test_budget_coverage` wraps every subprocess call site so a new one skipping `TickBudget.allows_call` fails; `test_tenant.py::test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` ratchets the single `except Exception` at `src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py:139`; `test_import_boundaries.py` rules 10/11 pin the layering; and the crash-recovery suite kills a real process at four points of the launch sequence and asserts the end state. Tests use throwaway stores under `tmp_path` only, with stub executables on `PATH` — no production-URL reads anywhere in the tier.

findings.title: Exception handling follows the project's swallow-with-justification rule
findings.description: Every `except` in the new modules is either specific-with-comment (`OSError`/`TimeoutExpired` in `probes.py` and `launch.py`, each justified as an expected external failure converted to an answer), or the one documented process-boundary catch in `tenant.py`. `finish.record` and `escalate` write their store side effects idempotently (block-once-then-resolve, dedup on `(project, kind)`), which the crash proof exercises directly.

structured_findings.summary: Legacy pre-120 `sq_run` entries without a run id can crash the resident process on the Runner's first tick
`_link` test helper is imported across test modules as a private name
Budget, fault and escalation discipline is mechanically enforced
Exception handling follows the project's swallow-with-justification rule
